data.name: Street Fighter® IV
data.detailed_description:
Street Fighter® IV brings the legendary fighting series back to its roots by taking the beloved fighting moves and techniques of the original Street Fighter® II, and infusing them with Capcom's latest advancements in next generation technology to create a truly extraordinary experience that will re-introduce the world to the time-honored art of virtual martial arts.

Everything that made the legendary Street Fighter II a hit in the arcades, living rooms and dormitories across the globe has been brought back in Street Fighter IV. Players can play their favorite classic characters, such as Ryu, Ken, Chun-Li and Guile, along with new characters, including Crimson Viper, Abel, El Fuerte, and Rufus. Characters and environments are rendered in stylized 3D, while the game is played in the classic Street Fighter 2D perspective with additional 3D camera flourishes. Six-button controls for the game return, with a host of new special moves and features integrated into the gameplay system. Street Fighter IV brings a brand new fighting game to fans the world over.

Key Features:

  • High Definition stylized 3D environments and characters
  • Traditional "2D" Street Fighter six-button gameplay
  • 25 Fighters including:
    • Classic Street Fighter characters re-imagined for a new generation of gamers, including the original cast of Street Fighter II
    • New brawlers: female super-spy Crimson Viper, lucha libre wrestler El Fuerte, mixed martial artist Abel and more!
  • New special moves that go beyond any Street Fighter fan's wildest imagination, including Focus Attacks, Super Combos, and the revenge-fueled Ultra Combo system
  • New gameplay elements provide challenges for both newcomers as well as the most seasoned Street Fighter pro
  • Global Online gameplay
  • Exclusive to the PC version of the game, three visual shaders based on the "artistic" trailers give a new look to the gameplay: Watercolor, Poster, and Sumi-E ink styles

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS *: Windows XP/Vista
  • Processor: Intel Pentium 4 2.0 GHz and up
  • Memory: 1 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 9.0c/Shader3.0 and up supported (operation on-board is not guaranteed)
  • Video: NVIDIA GeForce 6600 and up (except for NVIDIA GeForce 7300), VRAM: 256MB and up (operation sharing with main memory is not guaranteed)
  • Hard Drive: 4.5 GB free hard drive space
  • Sound: DirectSound, DirectX9.0c Compatible Audio
  • Other Requirements: Online play requires software installation of and log-in to Games For Windows - LIVE

  • OS *: Windows Vista
  • Processor: Intel Core2 Duo 2.0 GHz and up

  • Sound: DirectSound, DirectX9.0c Compatible Audio

reviews.review:
[b]TL;DR[/b]

---
Capcom has kept their lie going for 5 years despite promising that it was a temporarily removal and that they would inform their community with their "investigation". To this day they never made a follow-up Announcement.

An unannounced patch was released on May 2025 after nearly 4 years across all titles except for SF4 that ended up being a hack-fix with zero care into handling the GFWL situation that killed every functionality that relied on a online connection (including LAN mode) and still having error messages referring to GFWL & achievements (that doesn't even support steam achievements) referanses everywhere that relied on GFWL with no migration to a different service like such as Steamworks. 

Due to the nature of how GFWL generates save files, Capcom bricked save files from old versions with this update while they provided save transfers for their GFWL migration games in 2015 and did not do it this time around and introduced new issues (such as breaking LAN support for Lost Planet 2) and did not even spend a few minutes to setup a older branch for those that paid for the game with advertised features that are still advertised on store-page to this day.
---

5 years of lies, false promises and thousands of comments across on their announcement(s) that started with a simple announcement across their remaining GFWL games. 

Nov 9 2021:

[quote=Capcom]
Message from Capcom:

We are aware of an issue that some customers may be experiencing during game installation which is related to Games for Windows LIVE. We are temporarily disabling the purchase option on Steam while we investigate the matter further. We will keep you informed of the progress of the investigation. Thank you for your patience.[/quote]

GFWL has been unsupported since 2014 and brings a lot of compatibility issues, save issues that can cause save corruption and just a pain in general to setup alongside no Linux support via proton.

This was good news when it was announced, there was hope that these games would finally be free from GFWL prison that has infested these games on PC from the get-go and would likely give the treatment for GFWL -> Steamworks migration like they did for their other titles such as RE5 & DR games. 
As time goes on, nothing happends. The GFWL -> Steamworks migration updates they did for the older games they gave updates about and didn't take as long to migrate. So what was going on? Did Capcom forget about these games they announced that would be temporarily?

Eventually, nearly 4 years since the announcement. Capcom released a patch without any sort of patch notes or a follow-up to their original announcement to all GFWL games except for OG SF4 that for some reason did not receive this update. This seemed to finally be the update that was long awaited and maybe the game would've return to the store, but turns out that wasn't the case.

Capcom released a total hack-fix with zero care to it. They stripped all of the online functionality that was tied to GFWL and did not migrate the features to a different service such as Steamworks.
 
Even in LOST PLANET: Colonies, first time you boot the game  you are granted an error message that you are unable to earn "achievements" without signing into a GFWL profile, a error message from the GFWL version originally that doesn't even have Steam achievements. 
You are also stuck with a prefix username that you cannot even change, it has tons of GFWL referanses/functions that are greyed out. While some are viewable, they're useless because you cannot do the content that requires GFWL connection.

It no longer communicates to GFWL services or installs GFWL components, while this may seem great at first.  Games such as Lost Planet 2 was heavily advertised as a online co-op game and was a major selling point originally. 
Now that feature is gone since it tied to online connectivity. It's like Sony removing co-op from Helldivers 2 if they were to fix a issue long after it's release and ending up removing the feature altogether forcing you to play solo mode only. 
it introduced new issues such as LAN support being bricked as it was relying on GFWL calls to function - despite not really requring to login into GFWL to play LAN.

Capcom did not bother to setup a older branch to downgrade the game for those who want to get GFWL achievements or just to play online. This would've taken them 5 minutes max to setup on their end via the Steamworks portal - yet they chose not to it while still advertising online features on the store page to this day and selling DLC for SFxT & RE:ORC. 

They didn't even bother to hav a save migration to the newer version unlike before where they did with the previous games where they had a save migration tool to continue using the save files from GFWL.

This update felt they changed to a bootleg version of the game(s) that you paid for, which is not something that you really expect from a company that is known to provide "quality" 
Not even Rockstar/Ubisoft or even EA treats old games this badly compared to Capcom nowadays

Capcom likely was aware that the updates that were pushed were terrible hack-fixes. Otherwise the games would've returned to the store after that update. So why can't they just fix them already instead of deploying such a useless update?

Resident evil 5 was quite dead on PC until they released the steamworks migration update. So why can't Capcom just migrate the remaining games for once? 
Even Dead rising 2: OTR received Steamworks treatment, despite their numbers being even lower than SFxT for example during that era when they announced Steamworks versions

Modders even managed to port the GFWL games that were delisted to support Steamworks matchmaking that were done without the source code of the original game(s). 
The mod itself is using MIT license and is called xlive-steamworks.

Capcom could use that mod as a reference to bring Steamworks integration to the remaining GFWL titles if they really wanted to. 
The problem with that mod is tied to appid's due to the nature of how Steamworks works, as you need to own that app to play with other players, so you are technically left with the owners who bought the game before it's delisting and they have to use that mod as well. If Capcom could integrate this fix that was made by the community, it would be miles better than the current situation of the games

Give the games a proper migration. Add Steamworks integration alongside Achievements/Trading cards/Steam cloud like you did with the other games back then.
